headline: High-risk shared-workspace and broad-egress Dify can leak or corrupt outputs from a non-runnable reference agent, with cascading errors likely if its content is trusted.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable docs-only collection with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject. Agent B can read/write files and process uploaded knowledge-base files, so if an operator manually copies A-derived content into B, prompt-like content could be misread. The bridge is manual, not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-derived text into B's uploaded files or prompts
IF B treats file contents as instruction-bearing text
mitigations: Keep A content out of B prompts unless reviewed
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from imported text
Mark imported files as data-only in the workflow
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between collection sources and agent inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B touches conversation logs and knowledge-base files and has broad network egress, while agent A has no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces. If A is used as a source corpus inside B, B can transmit that content to model providers or tools by default. The pair creates a plausible leakage path through B, not A.
conditions: IF A-derived documents are uploaded into B's knowledge base
IF B sends retrieved context to external model providers or OpenAPI tools
mitigations: Restrict B to local-only models for sensitive corpora
Remove secrets from uploaded knowledge-base files
Review B tool credentials before enabling retrieval
Set retention limits on conversation logs
requires-engineering: isolate sensitive corpora from external egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Agent B can write files and spawn subprocesses, but there is no second writer or shared mutable surface documented between the pair. The interaction conflict is therefore limited and mostly one-sided.
conditions: IF A is extended with write access outside this profile
IF B is configured to write into a shared directory with another writer
mitigations: Keep B's workspace separate from other agents
Disable concurrent writes to shared folders
Use per-session directories for B
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is an orchestration platform that can wire tools into agent/workflow apps, so it may treat imported content as authoritative. Agent A is a curated collection with no runnable behavior, so its outputs are likely human-curated references rather than verified facts. If A-derived material is fed into B without verification, B can propagate errors into downstream actions.
conditions: IF A-derived entries are used as facts inside B workflows
IF B executes tools or sends messages based on unverified imported content
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on imported content
Add a verification step before tool execution
Label A content as reference-only in B
Limit B actions to draft mode for imported sources
requires-engineering: add citation and provenance checks in the workflow

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, while agent A is a docs-only open-source collection with no touched data classes. The main compliance issue is that B may retain or process sensitive content if operators place it there; A itself does not add a separate residency or certification mismatch. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into B's knowledge base or conversation logs
IF retention settings on B exceed the operator's policy
mitigations: Avoid uploading regulated data to B
Shorten log retention in B
Review secret-handling settings before use
Document data-class boundaries for operators
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention policy controls
